title: Yarn over
subtitle: The single hook movement that underpins every crochet stitch
excerpt: Yarn over is the action of wrapping the working yarn around the hook from back to front. Every stitch is built from yarn overs. Get the motion smooth and consistent and the stitches follow.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet chapter — yarn-over as the base action across all chain and stitch work.

glossaryTerms.definition: The tapered groove below the hook tip that grips the yarn during a yarn over. The throat depth varies between inline and tapered hook designs and affects how easily the yarn slides through.
The strand coming from the ball that you are actively crocheting with, as distinct from the tail end left from casting on or joining a new ball.

heroPrompt: Close-up of a hand holding a 4 mm crochet hook in cream DK cotton mid yarn-over — the yarn visible looping over the hook shaft from back to front, one loop already on the hook, against a pale grey background.

content.text: Yarn over is the single most repeated action in crochet. It means wrapping the
over the hook from back to front, so the yarn catches in the
. Every chain, every stitch, every technique is built from yarn overs and pull-throughs in different combinations. Getting this motion smooth makes everything downstream easier.
Hold the hook in the dominant hand. The yarn comes from the ball, over the index finger of the non-hook hand, and hangs down in front of the work.
Rotate the hook tip downward and toward you, bringing it under the strand of yarn that crosses your index finger.
Catch the yarn in the hook throat by rotating the tip back up. The yarn now sits in the groove.
Pull the hook (and the caught loop) through whatever you are entering — a chain space, a stitch top, a previous loop on the hook.

The yarn-tension hand controls how much yarn feeds through. Wrap the working yarn over the index finger, under the middle and ring fingers, and let it run from there to the ball. Raising the index finger tightens the feed; dropping it loosens the feed. Most crocheters adjust without thinking once the rhythm is established.
Do not grip the yarn tight with the yarn-tension hand. Guide it. The hook does the pulling; the yarn-tension hand controls the rate.

Yarn over goes from back to front. If you accidentally wrap front to back, the resulting loop sits twisted on the hook, and the stitch below will close with a twisted leg that looks different from the stitches on either side. If your stitches look inconsistent, check that every yarn over moves in the same direction.

attrs.title: How many yarn overs per stitch
attrs.body: Chain: 1 yarn over (pull through 1 loop). Double crochet: 2 yarn overs total. Half treble: 2 yarn overs before entering the stitch, then 1 more. Treble: 3 yarn overs total. Double treble: 4 yarn overs total. The pattern follows: each extra yarn over at the start adds one step to the close-down and raises the stitch by roughly 3-4 mm.
